Synopsis:
India's RBI is managing a record liquidity surplus of ₹9.70 trillion triggered by an oversubscribed $127.23B special dollar deposit scheme. The article outlines the RBI's toolkit to drain excess rupee liquidity: extended-tenor VRRRs, dollar-rupee sell-buy swaps, Market Stabilisation Scheme T-bills, CRR hikes (50-100 bps withdrawing ₹1.4-2.8T), and OMO bond sales. Each tool carries trade-offs — CRR hikes are blunt but effective, OMO sales push yields higher, and MSS faces government resistance due to interest cost. The core risk is that unabsorbed liquidity stokes already-rising inflation.
